webui.description: Browser UI served by `nanopi webui` (packages/webui, copied to dist/webui and embedded in single-file builds)

export-html.description: HTML export templates and vendored assets (dist/core/export-html)

docs.description: In-package documentation (embedded in single-file builds; the npm package always ships it)

examples.description: In-package examples (embedded in single-file builds; the npm package always ships them)

goal.description: Goal tracking module (planned; registered so its build wiring lands with the module)

toolset.description: Built-in tool set the build registers: "standard" (read, bash, edit, write plus the optional tools) or "bash" (the shell tools alone). Flavors set it as a name, not a switch; group keys like "module/*" work here too

providers.description: Provider set the build registers: one entry from the top-level "providerSets" map. The build's model catalogs are generated for that set only, so a trimmed build carries no code or data for the providers it drops. Flavors set it as a name, not a switch

module/extra.description: Run-mode, permission, and webui bridge module (packages/extra, @nanopi/pi-extra); a flavor that drops it aliases the module to an inert stub

module/codex-compaction.description: Codex-style compaction and its post-compaction warning

sidecar/tui-native.description: TUI native prebuilds builtin in single-file builds (all platforms embedded; the matching one installs to the agent bin directory, otherwise downloaded on demand)

sidecar/photon-wasm.description: photon wasm builtin in single-file builds (installed to the agent bin directory, otherwise downloaded on demand)

full.description: Everything included; the only flavor the npm packages are published from

base.description: Core CLI with the standard tool set (read, edit, write, bash), the preset model providers, and none of the bundled extras; no webui, export templates, sidecars, or OAuth flows

minimal.description: base with the bash tool alone and no built-in provider: the shell tool is the only tool the build registers, run modes and permissions (module/extra) are dropped with the extras, and the endpoint and key come from models.json instead of a shipped catalog

all.description: Every built-in provider catalog in packages/ai. The marker is checked against the generated catalogs at build time, and the model generator writes the concrete list back here once it writes more than one catalog, so a build never ships a provider the catalog does not have

none.description: No built-in provider at all: the model generator writes an empty catalog, the runtime registers no built-in provider, and the endpoint and key come from models.json. This is the minimal SKU, which is why the set is a value and not a switch

presets.description: The preset providers a standard deployment configures: one catalog per vendor the CLI can talk to out of the box. The full set has the same members today; the two part ways as soon as the catalog grows an internal or stand-in provider
